{{nihongo|'''Hyōsu Shrine'''|兵主神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Harima Province]].

'''Hyōsu Shrine''' (ひょうすじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} in {{ill|Kurodashō, Hyōgo|Q6446288|qid=Q6446288}} Oka, {{ill|Nishiwaki, Hyōgo|ar|نيشيواكا (هيوغو)|azb|نیشی‌واکی، هیوقو|ce|Нисиваки|ceb|Nishiwaki (lungsod sa Hapon)|de|Nishiwaki|es|Nishiwaki (Hyōgo)|fa|نیشی‌واکی، هیوگو|fi|Nishiwaki|fr|Nishiwaki|gl|Nishiwaki|it|Nishiwaki|ja|西脇市|ko|니시와키시|mg|Nishiwaki|mzn|نیشی‌واکی، هیوگو|nl|Nishiwaki|pl|Nishiwaki|pt|Nishiwaki|ro|Nishiwaki|ru|Нисиваки|sv|Nishiwaki|tg|Нишиваки|tl|Nishiwaki, Hyogo|tr|Nishiwaki|tt|Нисиваки|uk|Нісівакі|ur|نیشی واکی، ہیوگو|uz|Nishiwaki|vi|Nishiwaki, Hyōgo|war|Nishiwaki, Hyōgo|zh|西脇市|zh_classical|西脇市|zh_min_nan|Nisiwaki-chhī|zh_yue|西脇|qid=Q869020}}, {{ill|Hyōgo Prefecture|Q130290|qid=Q130290}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} and a former {{ill|Ken-sha|qid=Q90139226|lt=kensha}} under the old shrine ranking system. It is the {{ill|Ujigami|Q767655|qid=Q767655}} of the Ōshi-gō area<ref name="Nishiwaki official">{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.city.nishiwaki.lg.jp/kakukanogoannai/soumubu/hisyokouhouka/furusato/1435046702825.html|title=Hyōsu Shrine (Kurodashō-chō Oka)|publisher=Nishiwaki City|date=2015-06-23|accessdate=2020-12-13}}</ref>, and is locally known as "Hyōsu-san"<ref name="Nishiwaki tourism">{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.nishiwaki-kanko.jp/guide/history/hyosujinja.html|title=Hyōsu Shrine|publisher=Nishiwaki City Tourism Association|accessdate=2020-12-13}}</ref>.

=== History ===
The Hyōsu deity derives from the {{ill|Han dynasty|Q7209|qid=Q7209}}'s {{ill|Emperor Gaozu of Han|Q7210|qid=Q7210|lt=Emperor Gaozu}} enshrining "{{ill|Chiyou|Q1147255|qid=Q1147255}}" (Shiyū) and praying for victory. According to {{ill|Shigeki Kaizuka|Q11634459|qid=Q11634459}}, there is also the view that the deity was a {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=blacksmith deity}} — a {{ill|Deity|Q178885|qid=Q178885}} of {{ill|Weapon|Q728|qid=Q728}} manufacture.

According to shrine tradition, in {{ill|Enryaku|Q1373176|qid=Q1373176}} 1 ({{ill|782|Q30550|qid=Q30550}}), Okamoto Shuri-no-Taibu, who had been dispatched from {{ill|Yamato Province|Q907495|qid=Q907495}} to the {{ill|kokuga|Q11421342|qid=Q11421342}} of {{ill|Harima Province|Q1047523|qid=Q1047523}}, cleared forest and built the shrine buildings. Two years later, in Enryaku 3 ({{ill|784|Q30083|qid=Q30083}}), the {{ill|Anashi-Nimasu Hyōzu Shrine|Q11597229|qid=Q11597229|lt=Hyōsu deity of Yamato Anashi}} was invited (kanjō). According to 'Nihon no Kamigami 2,' '{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto Bunshin Ruishashō}}' records "Left seat: Yachihoko-no-Mikoto, also called Ōkuninushi-no-Mikoto, divine body is a broad spear, Hyōsu Izuhoko deity is this," from which it is inferred that by the {{ill|Middle Ages|Q12554|qid=Q12554}} the Hyōsu deity was associated with Yachihoko-no-Mikoto<ref name="kamnavi">[http://kamnavi.jp/ym/hiboko/kuroda.htm Kamnavi — Hyōsu Shrine (Kurodashō-chō)] accessed February 26, 2019</ref>.

=== Precinct ===
=== Architecture ===
The worship hall is a rare nationally notable example of thatched-roof ({{ill|Thatching|Q874531|qid=Q874531}}) {{ill|East Asian hip-and-gable roof|de|Irimoya|es|Tejado de gabletes de Asia oriental|fr|Irimoya-zukuri|ja|入母屋造|ko|팔작지붕|ru|Иримоя-дзукури|uk|Напіввальмовий дах|zh|歇山顶|qid=Q855025}} in the long-floor style with {{ill|Azuchi–Momoyama period|Q319531|qid=Q319531}} architectural features. According to the {{ill|Munafuda|ja|棟札|zh|上樑記牌|qid=Q8008834}}, it was renovated in {{ill|Tenshō (Momoyama period)|Q1145058|qid=Q1145058}} 19 ({{ill|1591|Q6766|qid=Q6766}})<ref name="Nishiwaki official" />. During the {{ill|Sengoku period|Q204023|qid=Q204023}}, when {{ill|Toyotomi Hideyoshi|Q187550|qid=Q187550|lt=Hashiba Hideyoshi}} attacked {{ill|Miki Castle|Q11242473|qid=Q11242473}} ({{ill|Bessho Nagaharu|Q837435|qid=Q837435}}), his retainer {{ill|Kuroda Yoshitaka|Q907019|qid=Q907019}} donated rice-field income for victory prayers, and the {{ill|Haiden (Shinto)|Q3125745|qid=Q3125745}} is said to have been renovated with those donated funds. In March {{ill|1977|Q2481|qid=Q2481}} (Shōwa 52), it was designated as an important cultural property of Hyōgo Prefecture<ref name="Nishiwaki official" />.

=== Festivals ===
Every October, the annual {{ill|Autumn Matsuri|Q11595783|qid=Q11595783}} is held. Five futon-yatai floats are paraded from the Ōbushi, Kita, Daimon, Tsumai, and Oka districts, and traditional events such as "Rekkei," which imitates a {{ill|daimyō gyōretsu|Q11433354|qid=Q11433354}}, are performed with great splendor. The floats enter the shrine precincts from around 11 AM on the main day. After the floats are set up in the precincts, children's dedicatory sumo is held; after mochi-throwing concludes around 2 PM, the floats depart. The festival was originally held on October 14 and 15, but the float procession and other festivities are now held on the second Saturday and Sunday of October<ref name="prosv8">{{Cite web|和書|url=http://prosv8.tok2.com/~harima/nisiwaki/hyousu.htm|title=Hyōsu Shrine Autumn Festival Introduction|accessdate=2018-10-7}}</ref><ref name="kamnavi" />.

Additionally, in {{ill|1983|Q2434|qid=Q2434}} ({{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 58), a grand festival commemorating the 1,200th anniversary of the shrine's founding (kanjō) was held.
